title: Course 11 Introduction to PySpark - 1000-Foot Opening Map
subtitle: DataCamp track kickoff plus Wipro interview sprint bridge

nodes.label: Why Spark Exists
nodes.definition: Spark processes data that may be too large or too slow for one-machine tools.
nodes.whyItMatters: It explains why distributed computing is needed for modern data workloads.
nodes.safeSentence: Spark is a distributed processing engine used for large-scale data processing.
nodes.commonTrap: Assuming one-machine tools are always enough.

note.summary: Spark exists for scale beyond single-machine limits.

nodes.label: What PySpark Is
nodes.definition: PySpark is the Python API for Apache Spark.
nodes.whyItMatters: It allows Python-based Spark DataFrame and SQL workflows.
nodes.safeSentence: PySpark lets me express Spark DataFrame and SQL work using Python.
nodes.commonTrap: Thinking PySpark is a separate engine.

note.summary: PySpark is Python control over Spark execution.

nodes.label: Driver
nodes.whyItMatters: It plans execution and orchestrates distributed tasks.
nodes.safeSentence: The driver coordinates Spark planning and execution.
nodes.commonTrap: Thinking the driver does all the data work.

note.summary: Driver is coordinator, not main data worker.

nodes.label: Executors
nodes.definition: Executors run tasks on partitions of data.
nodes.whyItMatters: Executor health affects performance and reliability.
nodes.safeSentence: Executors execute distributed tasks on partitioned data.
nodes.commonTrap: Ignoring executor failures or memory pressure.

note.summary: Executors perform the parallel data processing.

nodes.label: SparkSession
nodes.definition: SparkSession is the entry point for DataFrame and Spark SQL work.
nodes.whyItMatters: It sets runtime context and API access.
nodes.safeSentence: SparkSession is the main starting context for PySpark work.

nodes.label: DataFrame
nodes.definition: DataFrame is a table-like distributed data structure.
nodes.whyItMatters: Most ETL steps are implemented as DataFrame transformations.
nodes.safeSentence: A Spark DataFrame is distributed tabular data processed in parallel.
nodes.commonTrap: Treating it exactly like local Pandas.

note.summary: DataFrame operations are distributed, not local-only.

nodes.label: Transformations
nodes.definition: Transformations are lazy instructions like select, filter, withColumn, groupBy, and joins.
nodes.whyItMatters: They define the plan before execution.
nodes.safeSentence: Transformations describe work without immediate execution.

nodes.label: Actions
nodes.definition: Actions trigger execution, such as show, count, collect, and write.
nodes.whyItMatters: Actions launch cluster work and return results or outputs.
nodes.commonTrap: Using collect casually on large data.

note.summary: Actions execute lazy plans and require scale awareness.

nodes.label: Partitions and Shuffle
nodes.definition: Partitions split work; shuffle moves data across workers.
nodes.whyItMatters: These directly affect performance and cost.
nodes.safeSentence: Partitioning enables parallelism; shuffle is necessary but often expensive.
nodes.commonTrap: Ignoring expensive shuffles in joins and groupBy.

note.summary: Partition and shuffle behavior is core Spark tuning knowledge.

nodes.label: Production PySpark Job
nodes.definition: A real job needs validation, logs, counts, scheduling, rerun behavior, and support thinking.
nodes.whyItMatters: Production readiness means reliability and supportability.
nodes.safeSentence: Production PySpark combines correct logic with operational reliability.
nodes.commonTrap: Thinking success means code ran once.

note.summary: Production quality requires observability and repeatable operations.
